accepted.finding: Production CLI and MCP used a synthetic full-compatible generation instead of activating selected physical packages.
accepted.resolution: Both process entrypoints now await bootstrapFirstPartySurfaceGeneration; durable desired state and missing packages fail closed.

accepted.finding: A long-lived MCP server could retain compile-time availability after the canonical generation changed.
accepted.resolution: Every MCP list/call validates the process-pinned canonical pointer and returns restart-required mismatch before dispatch.

accepted.finding: Generated MCP descriptions could replace the established detailed tool descriptions with inventory IDs.
accepted.resolution: Generated metadata controls availability and ownership; the compatibility executor preserves its rich descriptions until its documented removal condition is met.

accepted.finding: Physical package activation order was lexical rather than dependency ordered.
accepted.resolution: Physical packages are now topologically activated with deterministic ASCII tie breaking and cycle/duplicate rejection.

refuted: CLI availability is checked after dynamic import; source checks before resolve().
Committed registration rollback leaks partial records; the commit catch disposes every successfully registered record in reverse order.
Successful registrations have no disposal path; physical mod disposers invoke the committed registrar disposers and tests prove all five projections empty.
CLI and Cesar names collide across registries; registry kinds and surfaces are separate namespaces.
A disabled JSON-RPC method must close the MCP connection; typed method refusal is the fail-closed behavior.
Missing selected documentation should fall back to unrelated docs; the frozen contract requires disabled docs generation to fail closed.
Hidden intent variants must all appear in slash help; discoverable slash actions and hidden parser variants are distinct generated categories.
open: The five temporary compatibility executors remain explicitly tracked and must be eliminated before final S9 acceptance.
Third-party folder-mod discovery and trust are intentionally deferred to S8 and were not accepted as an S6 defect.
